createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_inventory_records.created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ). Set to the UTC timestamp at the moment the record was inserted. Never changes (append-only table, no updates). Used to present the inventory history in chronological order.

IShoppingMallInventoryRecord.description: A single inventory record representing one discrete stock movement event in the append-only ledger for a product variant. Each record captures a signed quantity change, the reason for the change, an optional seller note for manual adjustments, and the event timestamp. Inventory records are immutable once created — they are never modified or deleted — ensuring a tamper-proof audit trail of all stock movements.
IShoppingMallInventoryRecord.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the shopping_mall_inventory_records table. All columns are mapped 1:1 with camelCase renaming: id → id, shopping_mall_product_variant_id → variantId, quantity → quantity, reason_type → reasonType, note → note, created_at → createdAt. The productVariant belongs-to relation is not included in this DTO; the FK column is exposed directly as variantId instead. This is an append-only, immutable table — no updated_at or deleted_at fields exist. Retrieve this record by joining shopping_mall_inventory_records on id and scoping to the correct shopping_mall_product_variant_id. reasonType must be one of: 'manual_restock', 'manual_adjustment', 'order_placement', 'order_cancellation', 'order_refund'. note is null for system-generated records (order_placement, order_cancellation, order_refund) and non-null for manual records (manual_restock, manual_adjustment).

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.description:
A single entry in a customer's personal wishlist, representing a product the customer has saved for future purchase consideration.

The wishlist item links the authenticated customer to a saved product at the product level (not variant-specific). It embeds a summary of the product at the time of retrieval, including the product name, primary image, price information, seller shop name, and category, so the customer can assess the product without navigating away from the wishlist.

Wishlist items are created when the customer adds a product and are removed automatically if the product is deleted. A customer cannot save the same product more than once; uniqueness is enforced per customer-product pair.

The product relation is resolved via JOIN on shopping_mall_product_id → shopping_mall_products and returned as IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary (includes name, primaryImageUrl, base_price, category, seller, created_at, deleted_at). The shopping_mall_customer_id column and customer relation are excluded because the actor identity is resolved from the authenticated JWT session and never exposed in read responses.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IRequest.description: Search criteria, status filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters for retrieving a paginated list of order items within a specific order. All fields are optional; omitting them returns all order items for the order with default sort (creation date ascending) and default pagination. Multiple status values may be combined to filter for items in any of those states simultaneously.

Represents the actual per-unit price the customer will pay for this variant.

updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cart_items.updated_at. ISO 8601 timestamp (with timezone) of the most recent modification, such as a quantity change or availability status update.

IShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.description: A lightweight summary of a single cart item belonging to the authenticated customer, returned as part of a paginated cart list. Each summary includes the selected product variant (with its SKU and option key-value pairs), the desired purchase quantity, the current availability status, and computed pricing fields. Items with non-available statuses remain visible so the customer can take appropriate action before checkout.
IShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Query shopping_mall_cart_items joined with shopping_mall_product_variants (via product_variant_id) and shopping_mall_product_variant_options (ordered by sequence ASC) to build the variant summary. Compute effective_price = COALESCE(variant.price_override, product.base_price). Compute subtotal = effective_price * quantity. Return results scoped to the authenticated customer's customer_id (resolved from JWT). Map productVariant relation to IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary.

IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and browsing the order list on the shopping mall platform.

All fields are optional. When no filters are specified, all accessible orders are returned — scoped to the authenticated customer's own orders, or platform-wide for administrators.

Supports filtering by order status, date range of order placement, and partial recipient name matching. Pagination controls allow configuring page size and navigating through result pages. Sort order defaults to most recently placed orders first.
IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
This is a filter and pagination request DTO for querying shopping_mall_orders. It is not directly mapped to a single database table but drives queries against the shopping_mall_orders table. Implementation:
- status: exact match WHERE status = :status on shopping_mall_orders.status column
- createdAtFrom: range filter WHERE created_at >= :createdAtFrom on shopping_mall_orders.created_at
- createdAtTo: range filter WHERE created_at <= :createdAtTo on shopping_mall_orders.created_at
- recipientName: trigram similarity search using GIN index on shopping_mall_orders.recipient_name (WHERE recipient_name ILIKE '%:recipientName%')
- sort: ORDER BY created_at ASC|DESC, default 'desc'
- page: 1-based page number, default 1
- limit: page size, default 20, max 100
Customer-scoping (WHERE shopping_mall_customer_id = authenticated customer id) is applied at the service layer based on JWT actor role; not part of this DTO. Admins/superAdmins see all orders without customer scoping. Results are returned wrapped in IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary with total count and page metadata.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description:
A lightweight summary representation of a shopping mall order, used in paginated list responses.

Each summary contains the essential fields needed for a customer or administrator to identify and review an order at a glance: the unique order identifier, the derived overall status, the total monetary amount, the recipient's name on the shipping address, the customer who placed the order, and the timestamp when the order was placed.

The `status` field is a derived, cached value computed from the aggregate statuses of all constituent order items. Possible values are `paid`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, `refunded`, and `partially_completed`.

Full shipping address details and order item breakdowns are not included in the summary; use the single-order retrieval endpoint to access complete order information.
IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Query shopping_mall_orders JOIN shopping_mall_customers via the customer relation (shopping_mall_customer_id FK). Return scalar columns: id, status, total_price (as totalPrice), recipient_name (as recipientName), created_at (as createdAt). Populate the customer field by joining shopping_mall_customers and returning an IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary object. Exclude all shipping address fields (address_line1, address_line2, city, state, postal_code, country), recipient_phone, updated_at, and all has-many relations (orderItems, shipments). Scope results by the authenticated customer's ID when the actor is a customer; return all orders when the actor is admin or superAdmin.

page.description: The page number to retrieve in the paginated result set (1-indexed). Defaults to the first page if not specified.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for offset-based pagination. Compute SQL offset as (page - 1) * limit. Defaults to 1 if omitted. Minimum value is 1.

limit.description: The maximum number of shipment records to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 if not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of shipment records to return per page. Used as the SQL LIMIT clause. Defaults to 20 if omitted. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.

carrier.description: Optional filter to narrow results to shipments from a specific logistics carrier. Supports partial text matching (e.g., 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL'). When omitted, all carriers are included.
carrier.x-autobe-specification: Optional partial text filter targeting the carrier column of shopping_mall_shipments. Applied as WHERE carrier ILIKE '%{carrier}%' when provided. Case-insensitive partial match. Omitting this field returns shipments regardless of carrier.

status.description: Optional filter by shipment lifecycle status. `pending` means the seller has not yet dispatched the shipment. `shipped` means the shipment has been dispatched but delivery has not been confirmed. `delivered` means the delivery has been confirmed. When omitted, all statuses are included.
status.x-autobe-specification: Optional derived lifecycle status filter targeting shopping_mall_shipments. Translates to SQL conditions: 'pending' → WHERE shipped_at IS NULL; 'shipped' → WHERE shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND delivered_at IS NULL; 'delivered' → WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL. When omitted, no status filter is applied and all active (non-deleted) shipments are returned.

IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.description: Pagination and optional filtering criteria for listing shipments associated with a specific order. All fields are optional — omitting them returns all active (non-deleted) shipments for the order in descending creation order. Use the `carrier` field to narrow results to a specific logistics provider, and the `status` field to filter by the derived shipment lifecycle state: `pending` (not yet dispatched), `shipped` (dispatched but not yet delivered), or `delivered` (confirmed delivery). The `orderId` context is provided via the URL path and should not be included in this request body.
IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This is the request/filter DTO for PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/orders/{orderId}/shipments. Query shopping_mall_shipments WHERE shopping_mall_order_id = {orderId from path} AND deleted_at IS NULL. Apply optional filters: carrier (WHERE carrier ILIKE '%{carrier}%'), status ('pending' → shipped_at IS NULL; 'shipped' → shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND delivered_at IS NULL; 'delivered' → delivered_at IS NOT NULL). Apply pagination: page (1-indexed, default=1) and limit (max=100, default=20) as standard offset-based pagination. Order results by created_at DESC.

status.description: Optional filter to restrict results to order items in a specific lifecycle status. When omitted or null, items of all statuses are returned. Valid values are: 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', and 'refunded'.
status.x-autobe-specification: Optional filter applied to shopping_mall_order_items.status during the JOIN query. When provided and non-null, adds a WHERE clause: shopping_mall_order_items.status = :status. Valid enum values: 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'. When null or omitted, no status filter is applied and items of all statuses are returned.

page.description: The 1-based page number to retrieve. Defaults to 1 (the first page) when not provided. Use in combination with limit to navigate through paginated results.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for pagination. Controls which page of results is returned. Default value is 1 when omitted. Used in conjunction with limit to calculate the SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit.

limit.description: The maximum number of shipment item records to return per page. Defaults to 20 when not specified. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Number of records to return per page. Default value is 20 when omitted. Minimum value is 1, maximum value is 100. Applied as the SQL LIMIT clause. Combined with page to compute OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IRequest.description: Request body for retrieving a paginated list of order items belonging to a specific shipment. Supports optional filtering by the order item's lifecycle status and standard pagination controls. All fields are optional — omitting them returns the full paginated result with default settings. The parent order and shipment are identified by path parameters, so this body focuses exclusively on filter and pagination criteria for the items within that shipment.
IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH endpoint that retrieves a paginated list of order items within a specific shipment. It does not map directly to a single database table. Implementation: query shopping_mall_shipment_items WHERE shopping_mall_shipment_id = :shipmentId (from path), JOIN shopping_mall_order_items ON shopping_mall_order_item_id = shopping_mall_order_items.id. Apply optional status filter on shopping_mall_order_items.status. Apply pagination using page (1-based, default 1) and limit (items per page, default 20, max 100). The orderId and shipmentId come from path parameters and must not be included in this DTO.

carrier.description: The name of the logistics carrier responsible for this shipment (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL). This field is required and must be a non-empty string. The carrier name is displayed to customers so they can identify which delivery service to contact for tracking inquiries.
carrier.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_shipments.carrier. Required non-empty string. Must have minLength: 1. Stores the name of the logistics carrier (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL) provided by the seller at the time of shipment update.

tracking_number.description: The carrier-assigned tracking number for this shipment. Customers use this code to monitor their delivery progress externally on the carrier's tracking website. May be `null` if a tracking number has not yet been assigned, or may be explicitly set to `null` to clear a previously recorded tracking code.
tracking_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_shipments.tracking_number. Nullable string. May be set to null to clear a previously assigned tracking code. Stores the carrier-assigned tracking number that customers use to monitor their delivery progress on the carrier's website.

shipped_at.description: The timestamp when the seller physically dispatched this shipment to the carrier. Set this field to record when the package left the seller's possession. If the shipment has not yet been dispatched, this field may be `null`. Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime string.
shipped_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_shipments.shipped_at. Nullable ISO 8601 datetime string. Represents the timestamp when the seller physically dispatched the package to the carrier. May be null if the dispatch has not yet been confirmed. Value is written as-is to the DB column (Timestamptz).

estimated_delivery_at.description: The projected date and time by which this shipment is expected to be delivered to the customer. This estimate is provided by the seller or carrier and is surfaced to the customer for planning purposes. May be `null` if no delivery estimate is available. Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime string.
estimated_delivery_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_shipments.estimated_delivery_at. Nullable ISO 8601 datetime string. Represents the projected delivery date and time provided by the seller or carrier. May be null if no estimate is available. Value is written as-is to the DB column (Timestamptz).

IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating the mutable logistics details of an existing shipment. A seller may update the carrier name, tracking number, dispatch timestamp, and estimated delivery date for a shipment they own. The `carrier` field is required; all other fields are optional and may be omitted if no change is needed. The `tracking_number` may be set to `null` to clear a previously assigned tracking code. The `shipped_at` timestamp records the moment the seller physically dispatched the package. The `estimated_delivery_at` field captures the projected delivery date supplied by the carrier or seller. Note: The `delivered_at` field cannot be set through this endpoint — it is managed separately by the delivery confirmation workflow.
IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update DTO mapping to shopping_mall_shipments table. Updatable columns accepted from the seller: carrier (required, non-empty string), tracking_number (optional, nullable string), shipped_at (optional, nullable ISO 8601 datetime for dispatch time), estimated_delivery_at (optional, nullable ISO 8601 datetime for projected delivery). On successful update, the service sets updated_at to the current timestamp automatically. Excluded: id (PK, system-managed), shopping_mall_order_id (path param), shopping_mall_seller_id (resolved from JWT), delivered_at (managed by the customer delivery confirmation workflow, not seller-editable), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed), and all relation objects (order, seller, shipmentItems).

reason.description: The customer's written explanation for requesting the cancellation of the specific order item. Must be a non-empty string. This reason is displayed to the responsible seller when they review the pending cancellation request.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Stored as the `reason` column in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`. The customer must supply a non-empty, non-whitespace text explaining why they want to cancel the order item. Backend validates minLength: 1 and rejects blank strings with a 422 error. The order item being cancelled is identified by `orderItemId` in the URL path — this `reason` field is the only user-provided field in the creation payload.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ICreate.description: Request body for submitting an administrator promotion request on the shopping mall platform. Authenticated customers or sellers use this DTO to formally apply for administrator status by providing a written reason text. All other fields (applicant identity, status, timestamps) are determined automatically by the server from the JWT session.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the request body for submitting an administrator promotion request. It maps to the creation workflow of an AdminRequest record (stored in a table such as `shopping_mall_admin_requests`, not directly in `shopping_mall_admins`). Only the `reason` field is user-provided; all other fields — applicant_type, applicant_id, status, id, created_at — are resolved server-side from the authenticated session or auto-generated. The backend trims the reason string before persisting. A user may only have one pending request at a time.

status.description: The seller's or administrator's resolution decision on the pending cancellation request. Set to 'approved' to accept the cancellation and transition the associated order item to 'cancelled', or 'rejected' to deny the cancellation and keep the order item in 'paid' status.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.status. The value must be either 'approved' (cancellation accepted; order item transitions to 'cancelled') or 'rejected' (cancellation denied; order item remains 'paid'). Only 'pending' requests can be transitioned. Validated server-side — any other value or an attempt to update a non-pending request results in a 422/409 error.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IUpdate.description: Request body for a seller or administrator to respond to a customer's pending cancellation request. Contains only the resolution decision — either 'approved' to accept the cancellation (transitioning the order item to 'cancelled') or 'rejected' to deny it. Only cancellation requests in 'pending' status can be acted upon. An immutable snapshot of this decision is automatically appended to the audit trail regardless of the outcome.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is used as the request body for PUT /shoppingMall/seller/cancellationRequests/{cancellationRequestId}. It contains only the `status` field, which the seller or administrator sets to either 'approved' or 'rejected'. The server resolves the caller identity from the JWT session. The cancellation request must currently be in 'pending' status; otherwise a 422/409 error is returned. On success, the server updates shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.status to the provided value and updated_at to the current timestamp. If approved, the associated shopping_mall_order_items.status is set to 'cancelled'. A new shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots record is created, copying the original reason verbatim from the cancellation request. The parent order status is then recalculated from all its order items' statuses.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Complete detail record of a customer order placed on the shopping mall platform.

An order is created when a customer completes checkout. It groups one or more order items (each representing a specific product variant purchased) and captures a permanent, immutable snapshot of the shipping address at the time of placement. The shipping address fields (recipient name, phone, address lines, city, state, postal code, and country) are stored inline and cannot be changed after the order is created — even if the customer later edits their saved address book.

The overall order status is a derived value computed from the aggregate statuses of all constituent order items. Possible values are: `paid`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, `refunded`, and `partially_completed`. This status is automatically recalculated whenever any child order item changes state.

The full detail includes the purchasing customer's summary profile, all order items with their immutable purchase snapshots (product name, variant options, price at purchase, seller shop name), and all associated shipments with carrier and tracking information.
IShoppingMallOrder.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_orders. Joins: customer via shopping_mall_customer_id → shopping_mall_customers (ISummary). HAS-MANY: orderItems via shopping_mall_order_items, shipments via shopping_mall_shipments. Nullable columns shipping_address_line2 and shipping_state map to oneOf[string, null] in required fields. status is a derived/cached string with values: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed. total_price is a double precision float sum of all order item (unit_price × quantity).

skuKeyword.description: Optional keyword to search product variants by SKU code. Partial, case-insensitive match is applied against the variant's unique SKU identifier.
skuKeyword.x-autobe-specification: When non-null, apply a case-insensitive partial match (ILIKE / GIN trigram index) on the shopping_mall_product_variants.sku column. E.g., skuKeyword='RED' matches 'VAR-RED-L', 'RED-001'. When null, no SKU filter is applied.

optionFilters.description: Optional list of option key-value pairs to filter variants by their configuration dimensions. All specified pairs must match conjunctively (e.g., [{ key: 'color', value: 'Red' }, { key: 'size', value: 'L' }] returns only Red/L variants). When omitted, variants are returned regardless of options.
optionFilters.x-autobe-specification: When non-null and non-empty, JOIN shopping_mall_product_variant_options on product_variant_id = shopping_mall_product_variants.id. For each { key, value } pair in optionFilters, an exact match on both the key and value columns is required (conjunctive AND). Only variants that satisfy all provided option pairs are returned. Each element is an IShoppingMallProductVariantOption.IRequest object. When null or empty, no option filtering is applied.

inStockOnly.description: When true, only variants with a positive current stock level (derived from aggregating inventory records) are returned. When false or omitted, variants are returned regardless of stock availability.
inStockOnly.x-autobe-specification: When true, restrict results to variants where SUM(quantity) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_records WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variants.id > 0. Computed via a subquery or GROUP BY aggregation on shopping_mall_inventory_records. When false or null, no stock filter is applied and all variants (including out-of-stock) are returned.

priceMin.description: Optional minimum effective price filter (inclusive). Applies to the variant's effective price: the variant-level price override when set, otherwise the parent product's base price.
priceMin.x-autobe-specification: When non-null, filter variants where COALESCE(shopping_mall_product_variants.price_override, shopping_mall_products.base_price) >= priceMin. Requires a JOIN on shopping_mall_products to resolve base_price when price_override is null. Must be >= 0.

priceMax.description: Optional maximum effective price filter (inclusive). Applies to the variant's effective price: the variant-level price override when set, otherwise the parent product's base price.
priceMax.x-autobe-specification: When non-null, filter variants where COALESCE(shopping_mall_product_variants.price_override, shopping_mall_products.base_price) <= priceMax. Requires a JOIN on shopping_mall_products to resolve base_price when price_override is null. Must be >= 0.

includeDeleted.description: When true, soft-deleted variants (those removed by the seller) are included in the results alongside active variants. Only available to the product's owning seller and administrators. Customers always see active variants only.
includeDeleted.x-autobe-specification: By default, only variants with deleted_at IS NULL in shopping_mall_product_variants are returned. When includeDeleted is true, remove the deleted_at IS NULL predicate so soft-deleted variants also appear. This flag is only honored if the authenticated actor is the seller who owns the product or an administrator. A non-owning seller setting includeDeleted=true must receive HTTP 403. When null or false, deleted_at IS NULL is always enforced.

sortField.description: The field to sort the variant list by. Accepts 'created_at' (creation date), 'sku' (SKU code alphabetically), or 'price' (effective price). Defaults to 'created_at' when omitted.
sortField.x-autobe-specification: Controls the ORDER BY column. Accepted values: 'created_at' -> ORDER BY shopping_mall_product_variants.created_at; 'sku' -> ORDER BY shopping_mall_product_variants.sku; 'price' -> ORDER BY COALESCE(shopping_mall_product_variants.price_override, shopping_mall_products.base_price). Default when null: 'created_at'.

sortOrder.description: The sort direction for the results. 'asc' returns the lowest values first; 'desc' returns the highest values first. Defaults to 'desc' (newest first) when omitted.
sortOrder.x-autobe-specification: Controls the sort direction of the ORDER BY clause. 'asc' -> ASC, 'desc' -> DESC. Default when null: 'desc' (most recently created first).

page.description: The page number to retrieve (1-based). Returns the corresponding page of paginated results. Defaults to page 1 when omitted.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for offset pagination. Offset is calculated as (page - 1) * limit. Default when null: 1. Must be >= 1.

limit.description: The maximum number of variants to return per page. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Maximum allowed value is 100.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of variants to return per page. Default when null: 20. Maximum allowed: 100. Must be >= 1.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IRequest.description: Search, filter, and pagination request body for listing product variants belonging to a specific product. All fields are optional. Supports filtering by SKU keyword, option key-value pairs, stock availability, price range, and soft-deleted state. Controls sort field and sort order, and provides pagination parameters.
IShoppingMallProductVariant.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is used as the request body for PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/variants. It drives a filtered, sorted, paginated query against the shopping_mall_product_variants table (joined with shopping_mall_product_variant_options for optionFilters, and aggregated against shopping_mall_inventory_records for stock checks). The productId path parameter scopes all queries to the relevant product. All fields are optional and nullable; omitting or nulling a field means that criterion is not applied. Default sort is created_at DESC, default page is 1, default limit is 20. The includeDeleted flag requires the requester to be either the owning seller or an administrator — a non-owning seller requesting includeDeleted=true must receive HTTP 403.

id.description: The unique identifier of this shipment item record, representing the association between a specific order item and its assigned shipment.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_shipment_items.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on insert.

shipmentId.description: The unique identifier of the shipment that this order item has been assigned to. Use this to correlate the shipment item back to its parent shipment record.
shipmentId.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_shipment_items.shopping_mall_shipment_id. The UUID of the parent shopping_mall_shipments record that this item belongs to.

orderItem.description: The full summary details of the order item that has been assigned to this shipment. Includes purchase quantity, unit price at checkout time, current lifecycle status, product variant information, and the immutable snapshot of the product and seller profile at the time of purchase.
orderItem.x-autobe-specification: Resolved by JOIN from shopping_mall_shipment_items.shopping_mall_order_item_id to shopping_mall_order_items.id. Returns a full IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary object including quantity, unit price, status, product variant summary, and the immutable order item snapshot.

createdAt.description: The timestamp indicating when this order item was assigned to the shipment. This marks the moment the seller grouped the order item into the shipment package for fulfillment.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_shipment_items.created_at. Set to the current timestamp (NOW()) at the moment the order item is assigned to the shipment. Immutable after creation.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.description: Represents a single shipment item record — the junction between a shipment and an individual order item within a seller's order fulfillment workflow. A shipment item is created when a seller assigns a paid order item to a specific shipment. Each order item can belong to at most one shipment at any point in time, enforced by a unique constraint on the order item reference. The creation timestamp records when the order item was grouped into the shipment. This DTO includes the identity of the parent shipment and the full summary details of the linked order item, providing a complete view of what is being shipped in a given fulfillment package.
IShoppingMallShipmentItem.x-autobe-specification: Fetch from shopping_mall_shipment_items by primary key (id), validated within the hierarchy orderId → shipmentId → shipmentItemId. JOIN shopping_mall_order_items ON shopping_mall_shipment_items.shopping_mall_order_item_id = shopping_mall_order_items.id to populate the nested orderItem field as IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary. The shopping_mall_shipment_id column is exposed as the scalar shipmentId UUID. The shipment context (order, seller) is resolved through path parameters and not repeated in the response body.

status.description: Optional filter to return only snapshots with the specified resolution decision. Accepted values are `'approved'` and `'rejected'`. When omitted, snapshots of all statuses are included.
status.x-autobe-specification: Optional filter on the `status` column of `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`. When provided, applies WHERE status = :status to the query. Valid values are 'approved' (seller approved the cancellation) and 'rejected' (seller rejected the cancellation). When null or omitted, snapshots of all statuses are returned.

keyword.description: Optional keyword to search within the cancellation reason text. Performs a partial-match search against the original customer-submitted reason recorded in each snapshot. When omitted, no text filtering is applied.
keyword.x-autobe-specification: Optional full-text/trigram search filter applied to the `reason` column of `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots` using the GIN index (pg_trgm). Implements ILIKE '%:keyword%' or similarity-based matching via pg_trgm. When null or omitted, no text filter is applied to the reason column.

from.description: Optional start of the date range filter (inclusive). Only snapshots created at or after this timestamp will be returned. When omitted, no lower date bound is applied.
from.x-autobe-specification: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the `created_at` date range filter on `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`. When provided, applies WHERE created_at >= :from to the query. Accepts ISO 8601 date-time string. When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied.

to.description: Optional end of the date range filter (inclusive). Only snapshots created at or before this timestamp will be returned. When omitted, no upper date bound is applied.
to.x-autobe-specification: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the `created_at` date range filter on `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`. When provided, applies WHERE created_at <= :to to the query. Accepts ISO 8601 date-time string. When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied.

page.description: Page number for paginated results (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 when not specified.
page.x-autobe-specification: Offset-based pagination page number (1-indexed). Used to calculate OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit against `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`. Defaults to 1 when null or omitted. Minimum value is 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshots to return per page. Defaults to 20 when not specified. Cannot exceed 100.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of snapshot records to return per page. Applied as LIMIT in the SQL query against `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`. Defaults to 20 when null or omitted. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestSnapshot.description: Request body for paginating, filtering, and searching the chronological snapshot history of a specific cancellation request. All fields are optional — when omitted, all snapshots for the given cancellation request are returned in ascending creation order. Filters can be freely combined.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequestSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the request body for PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/cancellationRequests/{cancellationRequestId}/snapshots. It represents the optional filter and pagination parameters used to query `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots` WHERE cancellation_request_id = :cancellationRequestId (from path). Apply optional filters: (1) status: WHERE status = :status; valid values are 'approved' and 'rejected'. (2) keyword: trigram full-text search using GIN index on the `reason` column (pg_trgm ILIKE or similarity). (3) from/to: WHERE created_at >= :from AND created_at <= :to. Order results by created_at ASC by default. Apply offset-based pagination: page defaults to 1, limit defaults to 20, maximum limit is 100. All fields are optional and nullable; omitting them returns the full chronological list.

orderItemIds.description: An ordered list of unique identifiers (UUIDs) for the paid order items to be assigned to this shipment. Each ID results in a new shipment item record that permanently links the specified order item to the shipment. At least one ID must be provided, each must correspond to a `paid` order item owned by the authenticated seller, and no ID may already be assigned to another shipment.
orderItemIds.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the shopping_mall_order_item_id column of shopping_mall_shipment_items. One element in this array produces one INSERT into shopping_mall_shipment_items with shopping_mall_order_item_id = element value and shopping_mall_shipment_id = path parameter {shipmentId}. Uniqueness of shopping_mall_order_item_id is enforced by a DB unique constraint. Minimum 1 element required; an empty array is rejected. Format: UUID v4 strings.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ICreate.description: Request body for assigning one or more paid order items to a specific shipment. The seller specifies the UUIDs of the order items to group into this shipment; the system creates one shipment item record per listed order item. All specified items must be in `paid` status, must belong to the authenticated seller's products, and must not have been previously assigned to another shipment. An empty list is not permitted.
IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This is a Create DTO for the shopping_mall_shipment_items junction table. It is submitted as the request body for POST /shoppingMall/seller/orders/{orderId}/shipments/{shipmentId}/items. The shopping_mall_shipment_id is derived from the {shipmentId} path parameter and is not included in this DTO. Each UUID in orderItemIds corresponds to one shopping_mall_order_item_id and results in the creation of one new shopping_mall_shipment_items row. Constraints: (1) each order item must exist and belong to the specified orderId; (2) each order item must have status='paid'; (3) each order item's product must be owned by the authenticated seller; (4) each order item must not already have a record in shopping_mall_shipment_items (unique constraint). At least one ID must be supplied (minItems: 1). All inserts are performed within a single database transaction with created_at = NOW(). On success the handler also transitions each order item status from 'paid' to 'shipped'.

id.description: The unique identifier of this cancellation request snapshot. Each snapshot record has a distinct UUID.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots.id. UUID primary key, unique per snapshot record.

status.description: The resolution decision recorded at the moment this snapshot was created. Either 'approved' (the cancellation was accepted) or 'rejected' (the cancellation was denied).

An immutable, point-in-time record of an order item, capturing the exact product state, variant SKU selection, and seller shop profile as they existed at the moment the order was placed.

This snapshot serves as the authoritative, tamper-proof record of what the customer purchased, at what price, and from which seller — regardless of any subsequent changes or deletions to the underlying product, variant, or seller profile.

The snapshot includes the full product information (name, description, base price, category, and ordered images), the specific variant configuration selected by the customer (SKU code, price, and option key-value pairs such as color or size), and the seller's public shop profile (shop name, description, and logo). Eagerly JOIN shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots ON seller_profile_snapshot_id to produce the sellerProfileSnapshot object. The record is immutable — no updated_at or deleted_at exist. IShoppingMallShipment.description:
A shipment record representing a logistics dispatch created by a seller for one or more order items within an order.

Each shipment captures the carrier name, tracking number, and a chronological trail of timestamps: when the seller dispatched the package (`shipped_at`), the projected delivery date (`estimated_delivery_at`), and the confirmed delivery time (`delivered_at`). Multiple shipments may exist for a single order when items from multiple sellers are fulfilled independently, or when a seller dispatches their items in separate packages.

The `seller` field identifies which seller is responsible for this shipment. The `items` array contains all order items grouped under this shipment, including purchase-time snapshot information for accurate historical display.

Tracking information is visible to the customer as soon as the shipment is created. The `delivered_at` field is set through the customer delivery confirmation workflow and is not editable by the seller directly.

All nullable timestamp columns (tracking_number, shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, delivered_at, deleted_at) map to oneOf [string, null].

IShoppingMallCartItem.description:
Full detail representation of a shopping cart item belonging to the authenticated customer.

A cart item links a customer to a specific product variant they intend to purchase, recording the desired quantity and the current availability state of that variant. Unlike a wishlist item (which tracks interest at the product level), a cart item is always bound to a concrete variant — meaning a specific configuration of option values such as color and size.

The response includes the selected product variant details (SKU, options), the effective unit price for the variant (from the variant's price override, or the product's base price if no override is set), the desired purchase quantity, the computed subtotal, the current availability status, and a stock warning flag.

The `availabilityStatus` field reflects the purchasability of the variant at the time the cart is displayed. Possible values are `available` (the variant is purchasable), `out_of_stock` (the variant exists but has no remaining inventory), and `variant_deleted` (the seller has removed the variant). Non-available items are flagged rather than removed, allowing the customer to review and decide.

The `stockWarning` flag is set to `true` when the variant has some remaining stock but that stock is less than the quantity in the cart, alerting the customer that the full requested quantity may not be fulfillable at checkout.
IShoppingMallCartItem.x-autobe-specification: Primary table: shopping_mall_cart_items (id, quantity, availability_status, created_at, updated_at, customer_id, product_variant_id). JOIN shopping_mall_product_variants (sku, price_override, deleted_at) ON cart_items.product_variant_id = variants.id. JOIN shopping_mall_products (name, base_price) ON variants.shopping_mall_product_id = products.id. JOIN shopping_mall_product_variant_options ON variants.id for variant options ordered by sequence ASC. Compute unit_price: if price_override IS NOT NULL use price_override, else use products.base_price. Compute subtotal: unit_price × quantity. Compute stock_warning: SUM(delta) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_records WHERE product_variant_id = cart_item.product_variant_id; set stockWarning = true if SUM > 0 AND SUM < cart_item.quantity, else false. availability_status is read directly from the shopping_mall_cart_items record (values: 'available', 'out_of_stock', 'variant_deleted'). The productVariant field is populated from IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary joining variant fields and options. customer_id is not exposed — authenticated customer context only. Verify cart item ownership: customer_id must match authenticated customer's JWT identity.

The customer provides a written reason explaining why the refund is being requested. This reason is preserved verbatim for audit and dispute resolution purposes. All other fields — including the target order item reference, status, and timestamps — are derived from path parameters or managed automatically by the server. Eligibility is strictly enforced: the order item must be in 'delivered' status and the request must be submitted within 7 calendar days of delivery. Each order item may have at most one refund request.

Search criteria and pagination parameters for listing administrator promotion requests.

This request body is used exclusively by super administrators to retrieve a filtered and paginated list of AdminRequest records. An AdminRequest is a formal application submitted by a registered customer or seller who wishes to join the platform's administrator team.

All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, all admin requests are returned sorted by submission timestamp in descending order (most recent first). Filters can be freely combined to narrow results.

This is a pure filter/pagination DTO with no direct single-table mapping. Used as the request body for PATCH /shoppingMall/superAdmin/adminRequests. The implementing service must:
1. Join shopping_mall_admins with shopping_mall_admin_of_customers and shopping_mall_admin_of_sellers to reconstruct AdminRequest records and determine applicant type.
2. Apply optional filters: status (pending/approved/rejected), applicantType (customer/seller), from/to date range on created_at, search keyword via LIKE or trigram on the reason text column.

4. Return a paginated response (IPageIShoppingMallAdminRequest.ISummary) with pagination metadata and a data array of AdminRequest summaries.

IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary.description:
A lightweight summary of a shipment record, used within paginated shipment list responses for a given order.

Each shipment represents a physical delivery package dispatched by a seller for one or more order items from the same order. It captures the logistics carrier name, the carrier-assigned tracking number, and the lifecycle timestamps: when the shipment was created, when it was dispatched, the estimated delivery date, and when it was actually delivered.

The `seller` field identifies the seller responsible for this shipment. The `orderItems` array lists all order items bundled into this specific shipment, enabling customers to know exactly which products are being delivered together in one physical package.

Fields `trackingNumber`, `shippedAt`, `estimatedDeliveryAt`, and `deliveredAt` may be null if the corresponding event has not yet occurred or the information has not been provided.
IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Map shopping_mall_shipments columns directly to DTO fields. JOIN shopping_mall_sellers ON shopping_mall_seller_id = shopping_mall_sellers.id to populate the seller field as IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary. For orderItems: JOIN shopping_mall_shipment_items ON shopping_mall_shipment_id = shopping_mall_shipments.id, then for each shipment item JOIN shopping_mall_order_items and shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots to produce IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ISummary elements. Filter: only include records where deleted_at IS NULL (active shipments only). Nullable columns shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, delivered_at and tracking_number are returned as null when not yet set. shopping_mall_order_id is available via path parameter context and is not exposed as a DTO property. The deleted_at column is used only for soft-delete filtering and is never returned in the response.

IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new shipment on a specific order by an authenticated seller.

A shipment groups one or more of the seller's eligible order items (those in `paid` status and belonging to the seller's own products) to be dispatched together under a single logistics carrier and tracking number. Both `carrier` and `trackingNumber` are required — a shipment cannot be created without logistics identification. The `orderItemIds` list must contain at least one item ID; all items must belong to the parent order, be owned by the authenticated seller, and currently have `paid` status.

Optionally, the seller may specify the actual dispatch timestamp (`shippedAt`) and an estimated delivery date (`estimatedDeliveryAt`). The order ID is provided as a path parameter and the seller identity is derived from the authentication session — neither needs to be included in the request body.
IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to shopping_mall_shipments. Required fields: carrier → carrier column, tracking_number → tracking_number column, orderItemIds → used to create shopping_mall_shipment_items junction records linking each provided order_item_id to the new shipment. Optional fields: shippedAt → shipped_at column, estimatedDeliveryAt → estimated_delivery_at column. Excluded from body: shopping_mall_order_id (taken from path orderId), shopping_mall_seller_id (taken from JWT session), id (auto UUID), delivered_at (system-set), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed). All provided orderItemIds must belong to the order, belong to the authenticated seller's products, have status='paid', and not already be assigned to another shipment — validated before insert.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of an individual order line item, used in paginated list responses. Each summary captures the quantity and unit price recorded at checkout time (immutable), the current independent lifecycle status of the item, a reference to the product variant that was purchased, and the immutable order item snapshot that preserves the exact product name, variant SKU, and seller profile as they existed at the moment of purchase.

This type is returned by the order item listing endpoint and is designed for efficient rendering of multi-item order views. For full details including cancellation requests, refund requests, or review information, use the single-item detail endpoint.
IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct fields from shopping_mall_order_items: id, quantity, unit_price (→ unitPrice), status, created_at (→ createdAt), updated_at (→ updatedAt). JOIN shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots ON shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots.shopping_mall_order_item_id = shopping_mall_order_items.id to populate snapshot (1:1). JOIN shopping_mall_product_variants ON shopping_mall_product_variants.id = shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_product_variant_id to populate productVariant as ISummary. Exclude: shopping_mall_order_id (in path), HAS-MANY children (cancellationRequest, refundRequest, review, shipmentItem).

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ISummar.description:
A lightweight summary of an administrator promotion request, used in paginated list views accessible to super administrators.

Each AdminRequest is a formal application submitted by a registered customer or seller who wishes to join the platform's administrator team. The summary provides enough context for a super administrator to assess and triage requests: the applicant's identity (type, display name, and email), the written reason provided at submission, the current lifecycle status, and the submission timestamp.

Statuses follow a strict lifecycle: all requests begin as `pending` and are transitioned to either `approved` (granting administrator access) or `rejected` (leaving the applicant's role unchanged) by a super administrator. Once submitted, the reason text and other request fields are immutable.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ISummar.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is computed from a JOIN of the admin request records table with shopping_mall_customers and shopping_mall_sellers. Implementation steps: (1) Query the admin requests table (which holds id, applicant_customer_id or applicant_seller_id FK, reason, status, created_at). (2) Join with shopping_mall_admin_of_customers or shopping_mall_admin_of_sellers to determine applicant origin. (3) Join to shopping_mall_customers (for nickname as applicantName and email as applicantEmail) or shopping_mall_sellers (for shop_name as applicantName and email as applicantEmail) based on applicant type. (4) applicantType is derived from which FK is non-null (customer → 'customer', seller → 'seller'). This is used in paginated list responses for super administrator admin request review endpoints.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
Represents a single line item within a customer order on the shopping mall platform. Each order item captures the specific product variant purchased, the quantity, the unit price at the time of purchase, and the current lifecycle status which progresses independently from other items in the same order.

The item includes an immutable purchase snapshot (`snapshot`) that preserves the complete product, variant SKU, and seller profile state as they existed at the moment of order placement — ensuring an accurate historical record even if the product is later edited or deleted.

Optional associations include the shipment record (once the seller dispatches the item), and any cancellation or refund request the customer may have submitted. A review may also be linked if the customer has reviewed the product after delivery.

Status lifecycle: `pending` → `paid` → `shipped` → `delivered`; with `cancelled` and `refunded` as terminal states reachable from various points in the lifecycle.
IShoppingMallOrderItem.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_order_items table. Join shopping_mall_product_variants for productVariant (BELONGS-TO). Join shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots (1:1 on shopping_mall_order_item_id) for snapshot. Check shopping_mall_shipment_items where shopping_mall_order_item_id = itemId, then join shopping_mall_shipments for shipment (nullable). Check shopping_mall_cancellation_requests where shopping_mall_order_item_id = itemId for cancellationRequest (nullable). Check shopping_mall_refund_requests where shopping_mall_order_item_id = itemId for refundRequest (nullable). Check shopping_mall_reviews where shopping_mall_order_item_id = itemId for review (nullable).

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.description:
A formal refund request submitted by a customer for a delivered order item, representing a post-sale monetary dispute resolution workflow between the customer and the responsible seller.

A refund request can only be submitted for an order item that has reached 'delivered' status, within 7 calendar days of delivery. Each order item may have at most one refund request. The request captures the customer's written reason and progresses through statuses: 'pending' (awaiting seller response), 'approved' (refund processed; order item transitions to 'refunded'), or 'rejected' (order item remains 'delivered').

Each time the seller or an administrator responds to the refund request, an immutable snapshot record is appended to the `snapshots` array, forming a tamper-proof chronological audit trail of all refund decisions associated with this request.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to expose orderItem as IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary (replacing the order_item_id FK scalar). Join with shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots ordered by created_at ASC to populate the snapshots array. All fields from shopping_mall_refund_requests (id, reason, status, created_at, updated_at) are included directly.

status.description: The seller's or administrator's resolution decision for the pending refund request. Must be either 'approved' (to process the refund and restore inventory) or 'rejected' (to decline the refund while leaving the order item in 'delivered' status). Only 'pending' refund requests can be updated; this field cannot be changed once a decision has been recorded.

On commit: (a) 'approved' — sets order item status to 'refunded', restores inventory, recalculates order status; (b) 'rejected' — no further changes beyond updating the refund request record and appending the snapshot.

This note is preserved in the immutable audit trail snapshot created at the time of the response. It may be used to communicate the rationale for an approval or rejection to the customer. Providing a note is not required but is recommended for transparency and dispute resolution purposes.

When null or omitted, no note is recorded. This field is entirely optional and its absence does not affect the resolution workflow.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IUpdate.description: Request body for a seller or administrator to respond to a pending customer refund request. Supply the resolution status ('approved' or 'rejected') and an optional explanatory note. The refund request must currently be in 'pending' status — attempts to update an already-resolved request will be rejected. When approved, the associated order item transitions to 'refunded' and inventory is restored. When rejected, the order item remains 'delivered'. Each response action is permanently recorded as an immutable snapshot in the refund request's audit trail.
IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the request body for PUT /shoppingMall/seller/refundRequests/{refundRequestId}. It allows an authenticated seller or administrator to resolve a pending refund request. Implementation: (1) Read status from body and validate it is one of 'approved' or 'rejected'. (2) Update shopping_mall_refund_requests.status to the provided value and set updated_at = now(). (3) Insert a new shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots record referencing the refund request ID with created_at = now(). The optional note field is NOT stored on the shopping_mall_refund_requests row — it should be attached to or logged alongside the newly created snapshot for audit purposes (e.g., as an annotation or additional metadata). (4) If status is 'approved': transition the associated shopping_mall_order_items.status to 'refunded', restore inventory via an append-only positive quantity record in shopping_mall_inventory_records, and recalculate the parent order's derived status. (5) If status is 'rejected': no order item or inventory changes are made. The id comes from the URL path parameter refundRequestId. Excluded fields not accepted in the body: id (path param), reason (customer-submitted, immutable), order_item_id (structural, resolved from the DB record), created_at/updated_at (system-managed), orderItem (relation), snapshots (relation).

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description: Request body for placing a new order on the shopping mall platform. The customer must provide a complete shipping address (recipient name, phone number, and all address detail fields) along with a non-empty list of product variants and desired quantities to purchase. IShoppingMallRefundRequestSnapshot.description:
An immutable, point-in-time snapshot of a refund request, automatically recorded each time a seller submits a response — either an approval or a rejection — to a customer's refund request.

Each snapshot captures the exact state of the parent refund request at the moment the seller's decision was recorded, including the customer's original reason text, the resolution status at that point in time, and the precise timestamp when the snapshot was created. Because snapshots are strictly append-only and can never be modified or deleted after creation, this type provides a tamper-proof historical record of a single decision event in the refund lifecycle.

This type is used in dispute resolution workflows, audit trails, and compliance reviews. Customers can use it to verify that a seller's rejection or approval was correctly recorded. Sellers can use it to confirm the decisions they made. Administrators can use it to reconstruct the full sequence of events during platform-level oversight or dispute arbitration.

The ISummary includes the parent refund request's id, reason, status, created_at, and updated_at fields, enriching the snapshot with contextual information about the refund decision recorded at the moment this snapshot was created. This is a read-only entity; snapshots are never mutated after creation.

- customerId: WHERE customer_id = :customerId (FK filter on shopping_mall_reviews.customer_id)
- minRating: WHERE rating >= :minRating (1–5, on shopping_mall_reviews.rating)

- updatedAtFrom/updatedAtTo: WHERE updated_at >= :updatedAtFrom AND updated_at <= :updatedAtTo

Rating values in the source table are integers 1–5; the averaged result is a floating-point number in the range [1.0, 5.0] or null.

review_count.description: The total number of active, non-deleted purchase-verified customer reviews for this product. This count directly corresponds to the number of reviews used to compute the `average_rating`. A value of 0 means the product has no active reviews.

Represents the total number of active (non-deleted) reviews contributing to the average_rating calculation. Always a non-negative integer (minimum 0). Deleted reviews (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are fully excluded from this count regardless of when they were deleted.

IShoppingMallReviewStatistic.description: Aggregate review statistics for a specific product in the shopping mall platform. Contains the arithmetic mean of star ratings (1–5 scale) across all active non-deleted purchase-verified reviews, along with the total count of those reviews. When a product has no active reviews, `average_rating` is `null` to clearly distinguish 'no reviews yet' from a calculated average. Publicly accessible by any actor including unauthenticated guests.
IShoppingMallReviewStatistic.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is not mapped to a single database table. It is a computed aggregation derived at query time from the shopping_mall_reviews table. Implementation steps: (1) Validate that the productId path parameter corresponds to an existing, non-deleted product in shopping_mall_products (deleted_at IS NULL); return 404 if not found. (2) Query shopping_mall_reviews WHERE product_id = :productId AND deleted_at IS NULL. (3) COUNT(*) the matching rows to produce review_count. (4) If review_count > 0, compute AVG(rating) rounded to 2 decimal places to produce average_rating; otherwise set average_rating to null. (5) Return the scalar result — no pagination, no filtering beyond the product scope. No authentication required.

IShoppingMallOrder.IForceRefund.description:
Request body for the administrator force-refund action on an order. Allows platform administrators (both regular admins and super admins) to immediately refund one or more order items within a specific order, bypassing the standard customer-initiated refund request and seller approval workflow.

Administrators may either specify a list of exact order item UUIDs to refund via `orderItemIds`, or set `refundAll` to `true` to target all eligible items in the order at once. An optional `adminNote` may be provided to document the reason for the force-refund, recorded for audit purposes.

Items already in `cancelled` or `refunded` status are ineligible and will cause the entire request to be rejected with a validation error if targeted.
IShoppingMallOrder.IForceRefund.x-autobe-specification: This is a pure command DTO consumed by the administrative force-refund service layer. It does not map to any single database table — it is an input-only object that drives a multi-step transactional operation. Implementation logic: (1) If refundAll is true, all shopping_mall_order_items WHERE shopping_mall_order_id = {orderId} are targeted for refund, regardless of any orderItemIds provided. (2) If refundAll is false, only the items specified in orderItemIds are targeted; each must be verified to belong to the given order. (3) adminNote is optionally stored for audit purposes — it may be persisted as a note on created shopping_mall_inventory_records entries or in a separate admin action log. (4) Eligibility validation must reject items whose current status is 'cancelled' or 'refunded'. (5) All DB writes (item status updates, inventory record creation, order status recalculation) are performed in an atomic transaction.

IShoppingMallReview.description:
Represents a complete purchase-verified customer review for a product in the shopping mall platform.

Each review is anchored to a specific order item, enforcing a 1:1 constraint that guarantees only customers who have purchased and received the product can submit a review. The review includes a mandatory star rating (integer from 1 to 5), an optional free-text body, the reviewer's customer summary, the qualifying order item summary, and a full chronological history of snapshots capturing all edits made to the review.

Content changes are preserved as immutable snapshot records (see `snapshots`), enabling administrators to audit the full revision history for dispute resolution. The `deleted_at` field supports soft deletion — deleted reviews are hidden from public view but retained for audit purposes.

Join shopping_mall_order_items on order_item_id to populate the orderItem field (ISummary). Include product_id as scalar UUID. Join shopping_mall_review_snapshots on shopping_mall_review_id = id, ordered by created_at ASC, to populate the snapshots array. body is nullable (String? in DB). deleted_at is nullable (soft-delete). rating is integer 1-5.

IShoppingMallSellerApproval.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and browsing seller approval records on the shopping mall platform.

All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, all seller approval records are returned in the default order (most recently submitted first). Administrators can combine multiple filters to narrow results — for example, filtering by `status: "pending"` and a date range to find newly submitted registrations awaiting review.

Text search fields (`sellerEmail`, `shopName`, `sellerKeyword`) support case-insensitive partial matching. Date range filters use inclusive boundaries. A single seller may have multiple approval records over time due to resubmissions after rejection; each record appears as a separate entry in the results.

The `page` and `limit` fields control pagination. The `sort` field accepts a sort expression (e.g., `submittedAt:desc`, `reviewedAt:asc`) to control result ordering.
IShoppingMallSellerApproval.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This is a search/filter/pagination request DTO that does not map to a single database table. It is used to query shopping_mall_seller_approvals (joined with shopping_mall_sellers) with optional filter conditions. All fields are optional — omitting all returns all records in the default sort order (submitted_at DESC). Filters are applied as WHERE conditions; text search fields use ILIKE for case-insensitive partial matching; date range fields use inclusive >= / <= bounds. Pagination is page-based (1-indexed, default page=1, default limit=20, max limit=100). The sort field accepts expressions like 'submittedAt:desc' or 'reviewedAt:asc'.

status.description: The administrator's review decision for the seller registration request. Must be either 'approved' to grant the seller full platform access, or 'rejected' to deny the application. When 'rejected', a non-empty `rejection_reason` must also be provided.
status.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the `status` column of the seller approval tracking entity. Allowed input values are 'approved' and 'rejected' only (not 'pending' — this operation exclusively transitions a pending approval to a decided state). Controls platform access: 'approved' permits the seller to create products and conduct sales; 'rejected' denies platform access and records the rejection reason.

rejection_reason.description: The reason for rejecting the seller's registration application. Required as a non-empty string when `status` is 'rejected', so the seller understands the grounds for denial and can correct their submission before reapplying. Must be `null` when `status` is 'approved'.
rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the `rejection_reason` column of the seller approval tracking entity. Business rules: (1) When status='rejected', this field must be a non-empty string (minLength: 1 enforced); providing null or an empty string results in a 422 validation error. (2) When status='approved', this field must be null; passing a non-null value when approving is a validation error. The stored rejection reason is visible to the rejected seller so they understand the grounds for denial and can correct their submission before reapplying.

IShoppingMallSellerApproval.IUpdate.description:
Request body for an administrator to review and decide on a pending seller registration approval, transitioning its status to either 'approved' or 'rejected'.

When status is set to 'approved', the seller gains full platform selling access. When status is set to 'rejected', a non-empty `rejection_reason` must be provided. The seller may view this reason and resubmit their registration.

This request can only be applied to approvals currently in 'pending' status.
IShoppingMallSellerApproval.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the request body for PUT /shoppingMall/admin/sellerApprovals/{approvalId} and PUT /shoppingMall/superAdmin/sellerApprovals/{approvalId}. It updates the SellerApproval record identified by the path parameter `approvalId`. The two user-provided fields map to columns of the seller approval tracking entity (not enumerated as a standalone DB schema): `status` updates the status column (constrained to 'approved' or 'rejected'; 'pending' is not a valid input since this operation exclusively transitions from pending); `rejection_reason` updates the rejection_reason column (must be a non-empty string when status='rejected', must be null when status='approved'). Server-side automatically sets: `reviewed_at` to the current timestamp; `reviewed_by_admin_id` to the authenticated admin's ID from the JWT. The operation will fail with 422 if the approval record is already decided (not 'pending'), or if status='rejected' and rejection_reason is absent/empty.

priceOverride.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from shopping_mall_product_variants.price_override (nullable DoublePrecision/number). When null, the caller must fall back to the parent product's base price to determine the effective selling price for this variant.

stockQuantity.x-autobe-specification: Computed value: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(quantity), 0) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_records WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId. This aggregates the append-only inventory ledger. If no records exist, COALESCE ensures the result is 0. The value may be reduced by negative quantity adjustment records.

isAvailable.description: Indicates whether this variant is currently available for purchase. `true` when stock is greater than zero; `false` when the variant is out of stock.
isAvailable.x-autobe-specification: Derived value: isAvailable = (stockQuantity > 0). Computed after the stockQuantity aggregation. true when the variant has positive stock and is ready for purchase; false when stock is zero or below.

IShoppingMallProductVariantStock.description: Real-time stock level and availability status of a specific product variant. This response object is computed on demand by aggregating all inventory records for the variant. It provides the current purchasability signal (`isAvailable`), the total computed stock quantity, and contextual metadata including the variant's SKU code and optional price override.
IShoppingMallProductVariantStock.x-autobe-specification: Computed response DTO derived from two source tables: (1) shopping_mall_product_variants — provides the variant's id (→ variantId), sku, and price_override (→ priceOverride). (2) shopping_mall_inventory_records — stockQuantity is computed as SELECT COALESCE(SUM(quantity), 0) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_records WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId. productId comes from the parent product context (validated via shopping_mall_products.id). isAvailable is derived: stockQuantity > 0. Both product and variant must have deleted_at IS NULL before computing. This DTO is returned by GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/stock.

IShoppingMallSellerApproval.ICreate.description:
Request body for submitting a new seller approval request to the platform. This DTO is intentionally empty — all necessary information is derived server-side from the authenticated seller's JWT session and platform state. No client-provided fields are required.

This endpoint is used by sellers who wish to resubmit their registration after a previous rejection, or by newly registered sellers whose initial approval record was not automatically created. The server automatically sets the approval status to `pending`, records the submission timestamp, and links the record to the authenticated seller's account.

Upon successful submission, the response returns the newly created `IShoppingMallSellerApproval` record in `pending` status. The seller must wait for an administrator to review and decide on the request before they can list products or conduct commerce on the platform.
IShoppingMallSellerApproval.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
IShoppingMallSellerApproval.ICreate is used as the request body for POST /shoppingMall/seller/approvals. No fields are required from the client — the server derives all values:
- seller_id: extracted from the authenticated seller's JWT session
- status: always initialized to 'pending'
- submitted_at: set to current server timestamp
- rejection_reason: null (not yet reviewed)
- reviewed_at: null (not yet reviewed)
- reviewed_by_admin_id: null (not yet reviewed)

The object has no required properties. Implementation should validate:
1. The authenticated seller must not be banned (is_banned = false on shopping_mall_sellers).
2. The seller's most recent approval record must have status 'rejected' (or no prior record exists for initial submission).
3. A seller with a 'pending' or 'approved' current approval may not submit again.

Create the SellerApproval record atomically in a single database transaction.

id.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the primary key column (UUID) of the dedicated seller approval tracking table. Used to uniquely identify a specific SellerApproval record. Pass this value as the `approvalId` path parameter when retrieving or updating a specific approval record via GET or PUT endpoints.

seller.description: A summary of the seller account that submitted this approval request. Includes the seller's unique identifier, email address, shop name, and account status flags.
seller.x-autobe-specification: Computed by joining the approval tracking table's seller_id foreign key column to the shopping_mall_sellers table. Returns an IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary object with the seller's id, email, shop_name, isBanned, isSuspended, createdAt, and updatedAt. This relation is always non-null — every approval record belongs to exactly one seller.

status.description: The current administrative decision status of this approval record. One of: `pending` (awaiting review), `approved` (seller granted platform access), or `rejected` (seller denied registration).

Allowed values: 'pending' (awaiting administrator review), 'approved' (seller is authorized to operate on the platform), 'rejected' (seller's registration was denied). Status transitions: only 'pending' → 'approved' or 'pending' → 'rejected' are valid. A rejected seller may resubmit, creating a new approval record with 'pending' status.

This field is immutable after creation and provides the chronological audit trail for each registration attempt.

The administrator is required to provide this reason at review time if rejecting; the system enforces a non-empty value (minLength: 1).
